# Your first Archicad *Python script.*

A Tapir script is a Python file that sends JSON commands to Archicad. This one asks Archicad how many elements are selected, and runs from the Tapir palette.

## Install Tapir

Install the Tapir Add-On with the Tapir Installer, as [Get started](https://archicad-api.com/start/#install) shows, and start Archicad with a project open. The Tapir palette runs scripts with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), which brings the Python each script needs; if uv is not installed yet, Tapir offers to install it the first time you run a script.

## Make a folder with aclib

Make a folder for your scripts, for example `Documents/Tapir scripts`, and an `aclib` folder inside it. Download [`builtin-scripts/aclib/__init__.py`](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/aclib/__init__.py) into that `aclib` folder. `aclib` is the small helper of the built-in scripts: it sends a Tapir command to Archicad and returns the answer.

Documents/Tapir scriptsfolder

```
FirstScript.py
aclib/
    __init__.py
```

## Write the script

Save this as `FirstScript.py` in the folder. The two headers are those of the built-in scripts, described in [`builtin-scripts/README.md`](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/README.md): uv reads the first, and the palette shows `changes` as *Read only*. The last two lines are [`archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSelectedElements.py`](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSelectedElements.py), the example of [`GetSelectedElements`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetSelectedElements).

FirstScript.pyPython

```
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = []
# ///

# /// tapir
# changes = "read-only"
# ///

"""
First Script

Prints how many elements are selected in Archicad.
"""
import aclib

selectedElements = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetSelectedElements', {})['elements']
print ('{} elements are selected.'.format (len (selectedElements)))
```

## Run it from the palette

Add the folder to `localFolders` in `Documents/Tapir/config.json`, with the `displayName` *My scripts*, as [Get started](https://archicad-api.com/start/#marketplace) shows. Choose *Tapir Palette* from the *Tapir* menu, then *Reload scripts...* at the bottom of its script list.

Select a few elements in Archicad, pick *FirstScript (My scripts)* in the palette's list and click *Run Script*. The palette reports what the script prints, such as `3 elements are selected.` Edits to the file take effect the next time you run it.

The palette starts the script with `uv run --script FirstScript.py --port <port>`, and `aclib` reads `--port`, so the script talks to the Archicad whose palette started it. With Python installed, you can also run it yourself as `python FirstScript.py`; it then uses the first Archicad, on port 19723.

## Call another command

Every Tapir command is called the same way: its name and a dictionary of its parameters. These lines count the walls of the project with [`GetElementsByType`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementsByType):

FirstScript.pyPython

```
walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements']
print ('{} walls in the project.'.format (len (walls)))
```

[The command reference](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/) lists every command with its parameters, its response and an example like the one above. To send the commands without `aclib`, see [Write a script of your own](https://archicad-api.com/start/#python).
